correctness.rationale: The square and mixed coefficients are separately imposed; in any characteristic, a nonzero b_h forces all a_i=c_i=0, and for b=0 the coefficients are exactly those of det(sum t_i H_i). For a nonzero rank-one uv^T in the span, every other nonzero member shares its image or row line; members with opposite strict alternatives would sum to a rank-two matrix. This proves the union in all characteristics. The common-line loci are closed by projective incidence (also by stacked-matrix minors). On a chart with a selected nonzero column/row, recovering the common line or kernel by that column/row is rational, so the incidence map is birational, not merely generically injective in positive characteristic. The two rulings are incomparable for r>=2 (take two independent matrices in one ruling); neither lies in L, and L has points with b nonzero. Their dimensions are 3r+1 against 4r for L. The intersections reduce respectively to 2r free entries, rank-at-most-one 2-by-r arrays, and tuples in Hom(k^2/K,I) for a pair of lines; including f gives 3r, 2r+1, 2r+2, with the stated triple intersection. Over F_q, span ranks 0, 1 and 2 have respectively 1, (q+1)^2(q^r-1), and 2(q+1)(q^r-1)(q^r-q) ordered tuples before the q^r factor; L adds q^(4r)-q^(3r). In particular the rank-two term vanishes at r=1. The proof does not address scheme structure.
